title: Josephine Iyamu ("Madam Sandra"): Nigerian women trafficked to German brothels via Libya
summary: Josephine Iyamu, a London-based nurse known to victims as Madam Sandra, recruited five women from rural Nigeria, bound them with a juju oath ceremony, and had them taken overland across Africa, through Libya, by boat to Italy and on to Germany on false documents, demanding €30,000 to €38,000 each to be repaid through prostitution in brothels. The UK National Crime Agency arrested her at Heathrow in August 2017. A Birmingham Crown Court jury convicted her in June 2018 of Modern Slavery Act offences and perverting the course of justice; she was sentenced to 14 years in July 2018, increased to 18 years by the Court of Appeal in September 2018. It was the first UK conviction under the Modern Slavery Act for trafficking carried out entirely abroad.
